Context/Background:
Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second leading cause of male cancer-related deaths. To date, the strategy to develop therapies for PCa mainly focuses on blocking either the activity or the transcriptional targets of known oncogenes. While the PCa transcriptome has been studied for decades, we have little knowledge of the translatome. The importance of this post-transcriptional regulation is underscored by the realization that RNA transcript levels are a poor proxy for protein abundance.

Translation initiation is a tightly regulated step critical to maintain the accurate protein dosage of growth and survival factors in cells.Importantly, emerging studies show that translation factors act in a rapid, selective, and robust manner to control the production of specific proteins. One of the most important of those factors is the RNA-binding protein and translation factor eukaryotic initiation factor 4A (eIF4A), which helps to unwind structured 5′ UTRs to increase translation initiation of select mRNAs in cancer.

Pharmacologic inhibition of eIF4A with zotatifin, a clinical compound, suppressed tumor growth in vivo, reducing both primary tumor growth and metastasis.

To understand how the inhibitor works mechanistically, we investigated the effect of zotatifin on the PCa translatome and proteome after a short treatment, as translation is one of the most rapid steps of gene expression. We performed ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and MS after 6 h of zotatifin treatment in 22Rv1 cell xenografts in vivo. While MS analysis assesses the effect of zotatifin on the global protein landscape in tumors, Ribo-seq can capture translation efficiency genome-wide at single-nucleotide resolution. Ribo-seq analysis revealed 554 downregulated transcripts at the translational level (false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.01 and log2FC ≤ −0.3). On the other hand, MS analysis showed that 339 proteins were downregulated upon zotatifin treatment (p value < 0.05 and log2FC ≤ −0.2). Next, we analyzed genes that are downregulated at the translational level as well as at the protein level by cross-referencing the two datasets using less stringent cutoffs (Ribo-seq FDR < 0.05 and log2FC < 0 and MS p value < 0.05 and log2(FC) < 0).
Prompt: From the genes that are downregulated at both translational level and protein level, prioritize a few targets that are particularly relevant to prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context
- Study system and perturbation: Prostate cancer (PCa) investigated with zotatifin, an eIF4A inhibitor, in vivo using 22Rv1 cell xenografts treated for 6 hours. The study used ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) to measure translation efficiency and mass spectrometry (MS) to quantify protein abundance, aiming to identify genes downregulated at both translational and protein levels.
- Datasets and integration: two uploaded datasets from the Zotatifin study were used: Kuzuoglu-Ozturk_2025_Cancer_Cell_TableS1-MS.csv (protein-level downregulation) and Kuzuoglu-Ozturk_2025_Cancer_Cell_TableS1-RiboSeq.csv (translation-level downregulation). An inner-join on gene_name identified genes downregulated at both levels. The integrated list comprises 20 genes (example row set shown includes ODC1, CDK6, CRY1, HIF1A, NELL2, PTTG1IP, MAGEA1, SUB1, BNIP3, CDKN2C, TTLL5, SPG21, MLF2, CRISPLD1, LRIG3, NDUFA4L2, COLGALT2, DDOST, TNFRSF10D, LRIG3). This subset reflects concurrent decreases in translation and protein abundance upon zotatifin treatment.
- Bottom-line signal relevant to PCa: Within the dual-downregulated set, several genes with mechanistic relevance to PCa emerge (e.g., HIF1A, ODC1, CRY1) alongside broader cell-cycle and survival regulators (e.g., SUB1, BNIP3, CDKN2C, PTTG1IP, LRIG3). These targets provide a focused starting point for mechanistic interpretation of zotatifin’s translationally selective effects in PCa.

Keywords
- zotatifin, eIF4A, translation initiation, translatome, proteome, Ribo-seq, MS, translational downregulation, protein downregulation, prostate cancer, 22Rv1, translational efficiency, ribosome profiling, translational repression, oncogenic signaling, hypoxia response, cell cycle, apoptosis, RTK regulation.

Candidate Genes (3–8 plausible mechanistic PCa-relevant targets)
- HIF1A
- ODC1
- CRY1
- PTTG1IP
- MAGEA1
- SUB1
- BNIP3
- LRIG3

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)
Two compact tables (Up and Down). The integrated dataset identifies a sizable set of Down genes (downregulated at both translational and protein levels) and no clear Up set from this dual-down intersection.

Up (leading-edge candidates; observed not observed in dual-down set)
- Not observed

Down (genes downregulated at both translational and protein levels; direction: Down)
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s) |
|------|-----------|---------------|------------|
| HIF1A | Down | Hypoxia-inducible transcription factor regulating metabolism and angiogenesis | HIF-1 signaling; hypoxia response |
| ODC1 | Down | Ornithine decarboxylase; rate-limiting enzyme in polyamine biosynthesis | Polyamine biosynthesis; cell growth |
| CRY1 | Down | Circadian clock regulator; transcriptional/temporal control | Circadian rhythm; transcriptional regulation |
| NELL2 | Down | Neuronal development/signaling factor | Neural development; secreted signaling |
| PTTG1IP | Down | PTTG1-interacting protein; cell-cycle related regulator | Cell cycle; DNA replication |
| MAGEA1 | Down | Cancer/testis antigen; immunogenic target | Immunogenic/cancer-testis antigen pathways |
| SUB1 | Down | Transcriptional regulator with RNA-binding features | Transcriptional regulation; RNA processing |
| BNIP3 | Down | Pro-apoptotic BCL2 family member; mitochondrial pathway | Apoptosis; mitochondrial signaling |
| CDKN2C | Down | CDK inhibitor; cell-cycle regulator | Cell cycle control; G1/S transition |
| TTLL5 | Down | Tubulin tyrosine ligase-like; PTM of tubulin | Microtubule modification; cytoskeleton |
| SPG21 | Down | Spartin-family protein; trafficking/endosome dynamics | Vesicle trafficking; endosomal function |
| MLF2 | Down | Myeloid leukemia factor family member | Transcriptional regulation/unknown, context-dependent |
| CRISPLD1 | Down | Cysteine-rich secreted protein family member | Secretory/secretome pathways; extracellular signaling |
| LRIG3 | Down | Leucine-rich repeats and immunoglobulin-like domains 3; RTK regulator | RTK signaling; EGFR family regulation |

Note: Up genes were not observed in the integrated dual-down dataset; Down genes reflect concurrent reductions in translation and protein abundance after zotatifin treatment.

Comparisons
- Tissue context vs dual-modality signals: The integrated dual-down set arises in a PCa xenograft model (22Rv1) following short-term eIF4A inhibition, aligning with a selective translational shutdown of transcripts whose protein products also decline. Several leading-down genes (HIF1A, ODC1, CRY1) map to hypoxia response, metabolism, and cell-cycle pathways commonly implicated in PCa progression and therapy resistance. Absence of a robust Up set in this dual-down framework suggests a net suppression of a subset of growth/survival programs rather than global upregulation of compensatory pathways, though single-modality signals (translation-only or protein-only) were not the focus here.

Implications
- Therapeutic relevance: The dual-downregulated genes include nodes in hypoxia signaling (HIF1A) and polyamine metabolism (ODC1), both of which have been associated with PCa aggressiveness and metabolic adaptation. The concurrent suppression at both translation and protein levels strengthens the case that zotatifin disrupts core survival programs by limiting translation of key drivers and their protein products, potentially enhancing anti-tumor effects in PCa. Immune-related targets (MAGEA1) and RTK-regulatory components (LRIG3) may also contribute to altered tumor-immune interactions and signaling dynamics, with potential combinatorial therapy implications.

Next Steps & Clarification
- Experimental validation: Confirm the presence and extent of dual-down regulation for each listed gene across replicates and additional PCa models (other cell lines and primary PCa samples).
- Mechanistic dissection: Determine whether the observed dual-down regulation results from reduced translation initiation via eIF4A suppression or from downstream decay of proteins and mRNAs due to feedback mechanisms.
- Functional testing: Assess the impact of selectively restoring individual dual-down targets (e.g., HIF1A, ODC1) on zotatifin sensitivity to distinguish which nodes drive anti-tumor effects.
- Therapeutic exploration: Evaluate combinatorial strategies pairing zotatifin with inhibitors targeting ODC1/polyamine metabolism or HIF1A-regulated processes to exploit convergent vulnerabilities in PCa.

References
- Validated in-steps references not provided here. No PMIDs included because stepwise validation was not performed within this exchange.
